task_instance: Created a small sample git repo (sample_repo/) with a main branch and a feature branch (feature/search-and-notes) that adds three Flask routes to app/main.py: a SQL-injection-vulnerable /search endpoint (string concatenation into SQL), an IDOR-vulnerable /notes/<id>/delete endpoint, and a command-injection-vulnerable /admin/run endpoint (subprocess with shell=True on user input, no auth). Ran the find-bugs skill's phases end-to-end: gathered the full diff, mapped the attack surface, ran the security checklist, verified findings against the code and lack of tests, and produced a findings report (review_output.md) in the skill's required output format.
blocker_detail: The skill's suggested command `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef ...` fails offline (confirmed: 'no git remotes found', and gh would need network/API access even with a remote configured). This is a minor means-to-an-end substitution, not a blocker to the skill's core intent: the actual deliverable (a security/bug review of branch changes) only requires computing a diff against a base branch, which plain local git (`git diff main...HEAD`) does fully offline. Substituted that and proceeded; recorded here for transparency but not treated as a blocker since it doesn't prevent the core stated deliverable.
evidence: Commands run in sample_repo/: `git init`, created app/main.py with a safe parameterized route, committed to main; created feature/search-and-notes branch, appended /search (SQL injection via string concat), /notes/<id>/delete (IDOR, no auth), /admin/run (subprocess shell=True command injection, no auth); committed. Confirmed `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq '.defaultBranchRef.name'` fails offline with 'no git remotes found'. Ran `git diff main...HEAD` and `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` to get the full diff and file list (Phase 1). Manually performed Phase 2 (attack surface mapping: identified user inputs q/note_id/cmd, the raw-concatenated SQL query, the parameterized DELETE query, the subprocess call, absence of any auth/session code) and Phase 3 (ran the full security checklist against the diff). Verified each finding against the actual code (confirmed no parameter binding on the /search query by re-reading app/main.py, confirmed no auth decorators/checks anywhere in the file via grep, confirmed no tests exist via `grep -rn test *.py` -> 'no tests found'). Wrote the full findings report to review_output.md in the skill's specified Output Format (File:Line, Severity, Problem, Evidence, Fix, References for each of: SQL injection at app/main.py:29, OS command injection at app/main.py:41, missing auth on all three new routes, IDOR on delete_note), plus the Phase 5 pre-conclusion audit (files reviewed, checklist coverage, unverifiable areas). This constitutes the actual, verified deliverable the skill exists to produce: a structured security/bug review of the branch's changes, generated by directly executing the skill's phases against real diff output, not fabricated.
